# Ultrastable (SAFE NOW)

**Ultrastable is the foundation for any autonomous system.**

Ultrastable creates and destroys its own parts to stay stable: inside its boundary the system has complete control to build, replace, delete and rebuild itself, and the boundary, not a permission prompt, keeps a failure from reaching anything outside it (`python3 -m foundation doctrine --check`).

A system is autonomous if it has self-referential loops and the ability to close them. Knowing without being able to act is useless, so the system is privileged to close its own loops (`python3 -m foundation loops --verify`).

**Ultrastable runs on itself.** Its own planning, work tracking and reporting are run by the system it gives to others.

**Coding agents write code. Ultrastable runs the system.**

Ultrastable is an autonomous system that sets up and runs any organized effort from one idea. The effort can be a company, an open-source project, a community or a lab. It bootstraps what the effort needs: development, branding, a provisional-patent filing package, a plan, search and analytics setup, promotion and outreach to funders. Then it keeps improving itself.

It is self-directed with light input. You can steer whenever you like, and it manages itself the rest of the time, so you do not need a development team, a patent lawyer or a marketing firm to start. Only decisions that cannot be undone come to a person.

**Why loops, not a prompt.** Vibe coding gets you a first draft. A system is something else: many agents, each with one job, running in code loops that check and improve their own work, with the rules written as code too. That is how Ultrastable is built: multi-agent, self-referential loops, not a single code agent.

**Who it is for:** people with ideas, founders, maintainers and small teams who want to get from idea to a running effort without hiring a team for each function. Commercial and open-source routes both stay open.

**What it is not:** it does not handle finances (accounting, payments, banking). Legal and patent outputs are drafts for professional review, not legal advice.

**Where it stands:** early. It runs in production for one first test case; we are looking for a few design partners. Figures about its performance are self-reported and not independently audited.

**Runs on:** the major clouds; built to be portable.

Licensing: source-available, free for non-commercial use, a commercial license for anything that makes money. Contact: pilot@ultrastable.io
